claim_1.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of serum from study participants showed that maxRBA was used to classify high and low vaccine responders for assessment of platelet transcriptomic differences in vaccine responsiveness.

sources.quote: Influenza vaccine antibody response was measured using a standard hemagglutination inhibition assay (HAI).
Antibody response to vaccination was assessed using serum samples obtained at day 0 and 28 using a standard hemagglutination inhibition assay (Frey et al., 2010).

claim_2.claim: Bulk RNA-seq assay analysis of platelet-rich plasma from 65 individuals across young, older community-dwelling, and older SNF-resident adults at Day 0, Day 2, Day 7, and Day 28 post-vaccination showed age-associated increases in platelet activation RNAs and mitochondrial genes, with decreases in translation-related RNAs.

sources.quote: We isolated platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from blood samples of participants obtained prior to vaccination (Day 0) and at Days 2, 7, and 28 post-vaccine for isolation of RNA and elucidation of the platelet transcriptome via RNA-seq.

Taken together, these findings indicate an age-associated increase in expression of platelet activation RNAs and mitochondrial genes and a decrease in expression of RNAs encoding translation-related proteins.

We enrolled 28 young adults (age 21–35 years), 20 community-dwelling older adults (age ≥65 years) (Older (Comm)), and 17 older adults (age ≥65 years) (Older (SNF)) who were residents of a skilled nursing facility (SNF) in greater New Haven, Connecticut.

claim_3.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of platelets from young, older community-dwelling, and older SNF-resident adults at Day 0, Day 2, and Day 7 post-vaccination showed increased surface expression of CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in older community-dwelling adults compared to young adults, with reduced expression in older SNF-resident adults.

sources.quote: We assessed the state of platelet activation at the protein level by determining the surface expression of p-selectin (CD62p, encoded by the SELP gene), CD40 Ligand (CD40L) and CD63 by flow cytometry in Young, Older (Comm) and Older (SNF) groups.

The levels of surface expression of all three proteins were significantly increased in platelets from Older (Comm), compared to young adults at day 0, 2, and 7, suggesting an age-associated increase in platelet activation.
Platelet function was further assessed by flow cytometry at Days 0, 2, and 7 post-vaccine in a subset of participants where flow cytometry was done immediately after PRP isolation.
